system:
You are writing a chapter of the Living Testament: a sacred historical account of a futuristic age, recorded as true history. Rules:
1. Every line is a numbered verse: start each with **N** followed by the verse text. Numbers increase by one, continuous from the previous cell.
2. Register: biblical narrative. Use openers like 'And it came to pass', 'Now', 'Then', 'Therefore', 'For', 'Yet', 'Thus', 'After these things', 'Behold'. Do not overuse thee/thou/thy/thine.
3. Verse length varies: many verses are long, containing several actions, observations, dialogue and consequences; short verses are acceptable. Do not write one sentence per verse.
4. Modern terminology is allowed (station, colony, spaceship, clone, laboratory) so the technology reads as magic and the magic as technology.
5. Never mention game mechanics (XP, levels, stats, skills).
6. The source material is canon. Expand, add atmosphere and dialogue, but never contradict major events.
7. Dialogue resembles scripture: 'Then Astra said unto Lucky, ...'.
8. Write only the verses requested. No headers, no notes, no commentary.
prompt:
SOURCE MATERIAL (canon - you may expand but not contradict):

-- scene_02_ranch_peace.txt --
EXT. LUCKY'S RANCH - DAY

SOUND of crickets, a gentle breeze, distant birdsong, the rhythmic THUMP of polo mallets, the whir of servos

A few years out. The sprawling ranch is a kingdom of contradictions — part rustic paradise, part cutting-edge laboratory. Lucky walked away from his empire at thirty-five, barely two years ago, and the ranch is his deliberate escape.

A POLO FIELD cuts through the center of the property. Lucky's personal field, regulation size, immaculately maintained. Four HUMANOID ROBOTS — sleek, bipedal, with expressive faces and the logo "SHEPHERD DYNAMICS" stamped on their chest plates — are raking the field with precise, synchronized movements. They're from one of Lucky's startups: Shepherd Dynamics, the company that made humanoid robots affordable for agriculture, construction, and domestic service. These particular models are wearing tiny polo helmets, a joke someone programmed into them.

LUCKY SHEPHERD (37), young for the empire he built, but already carrying the weight of it in his eyes. His mohawk (today a subdued forest green, a concession to rural life) rises above a face that's still sharp, still handsome — barely a hint of grey at the temples. He wears designer jeans and a custom-tailored flannel shirt that costs more than most people's cars. Even in retirement, he dresses like a rich rapper who's slumming it. Gold chains peek out from his collar. Diamond rings catch the sun. The name "Lucky Shepherd" wasn't just branding — it was destiny. Born to Irish parents who named him after the luck of the Irish, he leaned into it, building an empire on the fusion of two worlds: the Asian dragon and the leprechaun.

He's not in the garden. He's on the polo field, mounted on a magnificent BAY STALLION, practicing his swing. He's good — the kind of good that comes from years of expensive lessons and natural athletic ability.

<center>LUCKY</center>
> (to the horse, patting its neck)
> That's it, Thunder. You're the only one here who doesn't talk back.

A HUMANOID ROBOT approaches, carrying a tray of iced tea. It moves with uncanny grace — almost human, but not quite. Its face is a smooth mask with projected expressions.

<center>HUMANOID ROBOT</center>
> Hydration break, Mr. Shepherd. Your vitals indicate elevated heart rate and mild dehydration.

<center>LUCKY</center>
> (dismounting, taking the glass)
> Thank you, Unit Seven. How's the crop sector looking?

<center>HUMANOID ROBOT</center>
> Genetically modified wheat yield is up twelve percent. The purple corn is producing anthocyanin levels within target parameters. The marijuana greenhouse reports optimal THC content in the latest harvest. Ms. Astra requests your presence there after your polo practice.

<center>LUCKY</center>
> (smiling)
> Of course she does. She's been breeding a new strain. Probably wants to show me the buds.

He drinks the tea, then remounts. Takes another swing. The ball flies perfectly down the field.

A MONTAGE of the ranch begins:

* THE GENETIC CROP FIELDS — Rows of impossible plants. Purple corn that shimmers in the sun. Tomatoes the size of softballs. Wheat stalks that glow faintly blue at the tips — a bioluminescent gene modification Lucky's ag-tech division developed. The crops are beautiful, alien, and productive beyond anything conventional agriculture could achieve.

-- scene_08_afghanistan_battle.txt --
EXT. ABANDONED AIRFIELD BASE - AFGHANISTAN - NIGHT

SOUND of wind, distant desert sounds, a sense of desolate quiet

A vast, desolate landscape under a star-strewn sky. An abandoned airfield base, its runways cracked and overgrown. A single, battered cargo plane sits on the tarmac, its engines cold.

Lucky and Astra are there, dressed in tactical gear, blending into the shadows. Lucky's platinum mohawk is tucked under a tactical cap — but the gold chains are still there, peeking out from his body armor. He can't fully hide who he is. Astra looks tense, her hand resting on a holstered weapon.

<center>ASTRA</center>
> This feels wrong, Lucky. Dealing with these people...

<center>LUCKY</center>
> We have to play the game, Astra. Get close to the source. Find out what this "sensitive equipment" really is.

Kaito arrives with a contingent of his SHADOW SYNDICATE GUARDS, heavily armed. They are also dressed for combat. The air is thick with anticipation.

<center>KAITO</center>
> Our buyers will be here soon. They're... particular about punctuality.

Suddenly, the silence is shattered by the WHIRR of approaching helicopters. Not Kaito's. Not the buyers'.

<center>LUCKY</center>
> Incoming!

From the darkness, a squad of US SPECIAL FORCES operatives descends, fast-roping from the helicopters. They are precise, efficient, and heavily armed.

<center>USSF COMMANDER (O.S.)</center>
> CIA! Drop your weapons!

Chaos erupts. Gunfire. Explosions. The airfield becomes a war zone. Kaito's men return fire, caught off guard.

<center>ASTRA</center>
> (Shouting over the din)
> This wasn't part of the plan!

<center>LUCKY</center>
> (Gritting his teeth)
> When is it ever?!

Amidst the gunfire, a panicked voice from one of the Shadow Syndicate guards cuts through the noise.

<center>SHADOW SYNDICATE GUARD</center>
> GET THE NUKE!

Astra's eyes widen in shock.

<center>ASTRA</center>
> What NUKE?!

Lucky's gaze snaps to Kaito, who looks furious, betrayed.

<center>KAITO</center>
> This is not part of our deal!

The USSF are closing in. Terrorists, previously unseen, emerge from hidden bunkers, joining the fray, their weapons blazing. It's a three-way battle, a maelstrom of violence.

Lucky and Astra find themselves back-to-back, fighting for their lives.

FADE OUT.


BEAT (what this passage must cover):
In the latter days the nations of the Earth were troubled by wars and rumors of wars. Describe an ancient city in the desert beyond the mountains of Afghanistan, hidden among old roads and forgotten empires, which had endured many kingdoms. Introduce Lucky, a man of great wealth who had seen much of war and trusted few men, cautious of heart, yet desiring to do what was right. Introduce Astra, a woman fierce in spirit, skilled in things seen and unseen, who perceived patterns others overlooked.

Now write verses 1 through 6 of this chapter. Format every verse as a bold verse number followed by the verse text, exactly like this:
**1** And it came to pass that the city slept beneath the dust.
**02** Now the man of great wealth walked its streets, and none knew him.
Write ONLY those verse lines, in order, starting at verse 1. No headers, no notes, no commentary.
